_readme: Round 3 for BLK-TCIP-INTERFACE-FLOOR, 2026-08-07. Round 2's Europe PMC sweep of the chemically-induced-transcriptional-proximity literature surfaced, in its own abstract, the input MISSING-3 asks for: 'A bivalent molecular glue linking lysine acetyltransferases to oncogene-induced cell death' (Nix et al., Cell 2026, PMID 42476129, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2026.06.037; bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2025.03.14.643404) states that 'The crystal structure of the chemically induced p300-BCL6 complex reveals how chance protein-protein interactions may be exploited to confer the potency and selectivity of KAT-TCIPs.' That is a STRUCTURALLY CHARACTERISED induced interface in a system whose readout is transcriptional/epigenetic - and on BCL6, the same effector this route already staged from 7LWG. Neither the Cell paper nor the preprint is open access at Europe PMC, so the ACCESSION is sought from RCSB itself rather than from the paper: RCSB's own search index is the authority on what is deposited, and an entry found this way is verified downstream from its own _struct.title and _entity.pdbx_description exactly like every other entry in the census.
_note_si: PMC's OA service answered, verbatim, "identifier 'PMC12851799' is not Open Access", and the /articles/instance/.../bin/ path answers 200 with an 85-character 'Preparing to download ...' interstitial. Those are two independent, quoted refusals from NCBI itself, not a fetch that merely failed.
_note_biorxiv: bioRxiv answered 429 (rate limited) to all three TRACER URLs in round 2, which is a retryable condition and not a refusal. Retried here alongside the KAT-TCIP preprint.
